items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: this package we had, Sister Thorpe, Peg Leg Bates, Timmie and Freddie, and the Ink Spots, and were in Lucky's Millinder's band.

ctx.x: I had the worst luck of any guy I ever met in my life.

No, I don't think so. I think I had the worst luck, because I'll tell you this story. We were traveling with the Ink Spots. The Ink Spots was owned by the same agency that owned Lucky's band, so we used to have a package -- and this package we had, Sister Thorpe, Peg Leg Bates, Timmie and Freddie, and the Ink Spots, and were in Lucky's Millinder's band. Well, the lead singer with the Ink Spots, Bill Kinney, [long] loved to gamble, and he had the idea that his loan money would always win, although I know of a…
So, I had a cousin of mine that was living in Detroit and who was a professional gambler, and he took me one night to the Norwood Hotel.
